items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: When we started again in the Monseigneur we had an Egyptian drummer named Francois.

ctx.x: Pastraudis closed the Monseigneur in August for the whole month. We went to the beach most every day and enjoyed the vacation. Mae Caurance had come to Alexandria a month after we arrived there. She and Edgar were living in the Syracuse Hotel where I had stayed my first time in Egypt. Eventually there was a three-room apartment on the ground floor of the hotel, so Joe Hayman and myself moved in with Mae and Spider. Later there was an apartment on the top floor of the hotel which was the eighth floor. Mae did the…

Burns bought a white packard sport car with a rumble seat from Pastraudis and we went to Cairo a few times and visited the first Memphis in the world. During the vacation Pastraudis decided that he didn't like Arthur Pay, so he had him put out of the country. Arthur went back to Holland. When we started again in the Monseigneur we had an Egyptian drummer named Francois. His parents must have been French and he was born in Egypt.

As Egypt was a protectorate of England, it was normal that there were many English familes of the Royal British Navy. We made the acquaintance of four soldiers; two of them played music in a military band and the other two were jazz fans.
